questions.question: The unit digit of 7¹⁰³ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cyclicity of base digit 7 is 4 (7, 9, 3, 1).

Divide exponent 103 by cyclicity 4.

103 ÷ 4 ⇒ Remainder = 3.

Unit digit = 7³ = 343 → 3.

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Expression is 7¹⁰³

Method: Unit digit calculation using cyclicity of powers.

⇒ 7¹ = 7 (Unit digit: 7)

⇒ 7² = 49 (Unit digit: 9)

⇒ 7³ = 343 (Unit digit: 3)

⇒ 7⁴ = 2401 (Unit digit: 1)

⇒ 7⁵ = 16807 (Unit digit: 7)

⇒ Since the unit digit repeats every 4 powers, cyclicity = 4.

⇒ Divide 103 by 4: 103 = (25 × 4) + 3

⇒ Unit digit of 7¹⁰³ = Unit digit of 7³

⇒ 7³ = 343

⇒ Required unit digit = 3

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclicity of Digits

Digits 0, 1, 5, 6 have cyclicity 1. Digits 4 and 9 have cyclicity 2. Digits 2, 3, 7, 8 have cyclicity 4.

Zero Remainder Rule

If the remainder of Exponent ÷ Cyclicity is 0, the unit digit is the same as baseCyclicity. For example, unit digit of 7¹⁰⁰ is 7⁴ → 1.

BODMAS in Unit Digits

When finding unit digits of sums or products, perform operations only on the unit digits of individual terms to save time.</p

questions.question: Evaluate: ((1)/(28)) + ((1)/(35)) + ((1)/(49)) + ((1)/(56))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of (28, 35, 49, 56) = 1960.

Convert all fractions to base 1960:

Sum = (70 + 56 + 40 + 35) ÷ 1960

Sum = 201 ÷ 1960

Value ≈ 0.102551...

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (1/28) + (1/35) + (1/49) + (1/56)

**Formula used:**

Addition of fractions = [Sum of (LCM ÷ denominator)] ÷ LCM

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of denominators:

⇒ 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ 35 = 5 × 7

⇒ 49 = 7²

⇒ 56 = 2³ × 7

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 5 × 7² = 8 × 5 × 49 = 1960

⇒ (1/28) + (1/35) + (1/49) + (1/56) = (1960/28 + 1960/35 + 1960/49 + 1960/56) ÷ 1960

⇒ Sum = (70 + 56 + 40 + 35) ÷ 1960

⇒ Sum = 201 ÷ 1960

⇒ Sum ≈ 0.10255102...

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. It is used to create common denominators for fraction addition.

Prime Factorization Method

Find the highest power of every prime factor present in the numbers and multiply them to calculate the LCM efficiently.

Decimal Approximation

When options are close, carry out division to at least 4 or 5 decimal places to ensure accuracy.

questions.question: The average age of a group of 8 people increases by 2 years when a person aged 14 is replaced by a new person. Find the age of the new person.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Increase in age = Number of people × Increase in average

⇒ Total Increase = 8 × 2 = 16 years

Age of new person = Age of replaced person + Total Increase

⇒ New person age = 14 + 16 = 30 years

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of people = 8

Age of the person replaced = 14 years

Increase in average age = 2 years

**Formula:**

New value = Replaced value + (Total members × Increase in average)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial average age be A.

⇒ Total initial age = 8 × A

⇒ Let the age of the new person be N.

⇒ New total age = (8 × A) − 14 + N

⇒ New average = (8A − 14 + N) ÷ 8

⇒ According to the question: New average = A + 2

⇒ (8A − 14 + N) ÷ 8 = A + 2

⇒ 8A − 14 + N = 8(A + 2)

⇒ 8A − 14 + N = 8A + 16

⇒ N − 14 = 16

⇒ N = 16 + 14

⇒ N = 30 years

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Change Rule

If every quantity in a set is increased or decreased by a constant value k, the average of the set also increases or decreases by k.

Replacement Concept

In replacement problems, if the average increases, the new member is older than the replaced member. If the average decreases, the new member is younger.

Weighted Average Formula

Combined Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the number of items and x is the average of each group.

questions.question: The price of cooking oil increased by 8%. A family uses 12 litres of cooking oil per month. If the original price was ₹150 per litre, what is the additional annual expenditure (to the nearest Rs.) for the family due to the price hike?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price increase per litre = 8% of ₹150 = ₹12

Total litres used in a year = 12 litres/month × 12 months = 144 litres

Additional annual expenditure = Total annual litres × Price increase = 144 × 12 = ₹1,728

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original Price = ₹150/litre, Monthly usage = 12 litres, Price hike = 8%.

**Formula Used:** Additional Expenditure = Total Consumption × (New Price − Original Price)

⇒ Original price = ₹150

⇒ Increase in price = 8% of 150 = (8 ÷ 100) × 150 = ₹12

⇒ New price = 150 + 12 = ₹162

⇒ Annual consumption = 12 × 12 = 144 litres

⇒ Additional annual expenditure = Annual consumption × Price increase

⇒ Additional annual expenditure = 144 × 12 = ₹1,728

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Expenditure Formula

Total Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If any one factor changes, the total expenditure changes proportionally.

Constant Expenditure Rule

If the price of a commodity increases by r%, then the reduction in consumption to keep the expenditure same is [r ÷ (100 + r)] × 100%.

Percentage Change

New Value = Original Value × [1 + (Percentage Increase ÷ 100)]. For decrease, use the minus sign.

questions.question: A certain amount of money triples in 8 years under compound interest. How many years will it take for that amount to increase to nine times its original value?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In compound interest, if a sum becomes nx times in T₁ years and ny times in T₂ years, then T₁/x = T₂/y.

Sum triples (3¹ times) in 8 years → 3¹ → 8 years.

Sum becomes nine times (3² times) → 3² → 8 × 2 years.

Total time required = 16 years.

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

Effective Cost Price

When goods are lost or spoiled, the effective cost price per unit increases. Effective CP = Total CP ÷ Remaining Quantity.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Marked Price and Discount

questions.question:
A merchant mixes 60 kg of coffee at ₹90 /kg with a dearer variety at ₹120 /kg. He sells the blend at ₹110 /kg and gains 10 % profit.
How many kg of the dearer variety did he add?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of mixture = SP × 100 / (100 + Profit%) = 110 × 100/110 = ₹100/kg.

Using Alligation: Ratio of Cheaper to Dearer = (120 − 100) : (100 − 90) = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1.

Given, 2 units of cheaper variety = 60 kg.

∴ 1 unit of dearer variety = 30 kg.

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of variety 1 (Q₁) = 60 kg

Price of variety 1 (C₁) = ₹90 /kg

Price of variety 2 (C₂) = ₹120 /kg

Selling Price of mixture (SP) = ₹110 /kg

Profit percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP ÷ (1 + Profit%)

Alligation Ratio (Q₁ : Q₂) = (C₂ − CPₘᵢₓ) : (CPₘᵢₓ − C₁)

 Cheaper (C1)
 
 90
 Dearer (C2)
 
 120
 Mean (CP)

•

 Ratio = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of mixture = 110 ÷ (1 + 10/100) = 110 ÷ 1.1 = ₹100/kg

⇒ Ratio of quantity = (120 − 100) : (100 − 90)

⇒ Ratio = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1

⇒ According to the problem, Cheaper quantity (2 units) = 60 kg

⇒ 1 unit = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 kg

⇒ Quantity of dearer variety = 1 × 30 = 30 kg

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Method

It is a rule used to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at given prices must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired price.

Profit and CP Relation

If SP and Profit% are given, then CP = SP × [100 / (100 + Profit %)]. If Loss% is given, then CP = SP × [100 / (100 − Loss %)].

Weighted Average

The mean price of the mixture is the weighted average: CPₘᵢₓ = (n₁C₁ + n₂C₂) / (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: A can complete a job in 36 days. Every third day, he is assisted by B who can complete the job alone in 48 days. In how many days will the job be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(36, 48) = 144 units. Efficiencies: A = 4, B = 3.

3-day cycle: Day 1 (A) + Day 2 (A) + Day 3 (A+B) = 4 + 4 + 7 = 15 units.

In 9 cycles (27 days): 15 × 9 = 135 units. Remaining: 144 − 135 = 9 units.

Day 28: A completes 4 units. Remaining: 5 units.

Day 29: A completes 4 units. Remaining: 1 unit.

Day 30: A+B take 1/7 day to finish the last unit. Total = 29 ¹/₇ days.

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: A can do the work in 36 days. B can do the work in 48 days.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

 
 
 

 **Person**
 **Number of Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 36
 144 (LCM)
 144/36 = 4
 
 

 B
 48
 144/48 = 3
 
 
 
 
Work pattern: Day 1: A, Day 2: A, Day 3: (A+B)

 
⇒ Work in 3 days = 4 + 4 + (4 + 3) = 15 units

 
⇒ Work in 9 such cycles (27 days) = 15 × 9 = 135 units

 
⇒ Remaining work = 144 − 135 = 9 units

 
⇒ Work on 28th day (A) = 4 units. Remaining = 5 units

 
⇒ Work on 29th day (A) = 4 units. Remaining = 1 unit

 
⇒ Time for A+B to finish remaining 1 unit = 1 ÷ 7 = ¹/₇ day

 
⇒ Total time = 27 + 1 + 1 + ¹/₇ = 29 ¹/₇ days

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

When persons work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle of days and then find the number of full cycles needed.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person, which is proportional to (Efficiency × Time).

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to time and work, but use negative efficiency for outlet pipes (leakage) that empty the tank.</p

questions.question: A large ship consumes 0.2 liters of fuel per km, and a smaller ship consumes 0.15 liters per km. If the large ship travels 500 km and the small ship travels 400 km, what is the total fuel cost at a rate of ₹110 per liter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total fuel = (0.2 × 500) + (0.15 × 400)

Total fuel = 100 + 60 = 160 liters

Total cost = 160 × 110 = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Large ship rate = 0.2 L/km, Distance = 500 km

Small ship rate = 0.15 L/km, Distance = 400 km

Fuel price = ₹110 per liter

**Formula Used:**

Total Fuel = (Consumption rate₁ × Distance₁) + (Consumption rate₂ × Distance₂)

Total Cost = Total Fuel × Price per liter

 
 Large Ship
 500 km × 0.2 L/km
 = 100 Liters
 
 Small Ship
 400 km × 0.15 L/km
 = 60 Liters
 
• 
 Total Fuel = 100 + 60 = 160 L
 Total Cost = 160 × ₹110 = ₹17,600

⇒ Fuel consumed by large ship = 0.2 × 500 = 100 liters

⇒ Fuel consumed by small ship = 0.15 × 400 = 60 liters

⇒ Total fuel consumed by both ships = 100 + 60 = 160 liters

⇒ Cost of fuel per liter = ₹110

⇒ Total fuel cost = 160 × 110

⇒ Total fuel cost = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method for Consumption

Total consumption is calculated by multiplying the rate of consumption per unit distance by the total distance traveled (Fuel = Rate × Distance).

Total Cost Calculation

Total Cost = Total Quantity × Price per Unit. In this case, Quantity is the total fuel in liters and Price is the cost per liter.

Fuel Efficiency

Efficiency can also be expressed as distance per liter (km/L), which is the reciprocal of liters per km (L/km). Higher L/km means lower efficiency.

questions.question: If x + (1)/(x+2) = 6 , determine the value of (x + 2)³ + (1)/((x+2)³)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Add 2 to both sides of the equation: (x + 2) + 1/(x + 2) = 6 + 2 = 8.

This is now in the form k + 1/k = n, where k = (x + 2) and n = 8.

Shortcut formula for k³ + 1/k³ is n³ − 3n.

Required value = 8³ − 3 × 8 = 512 − 24 = 488.

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + 1/(x + 2) = 6

**Formula Used:**

If a + 1/a = k, then a³ + 1/a³ = k³ − 3k

**Calculations:**

⇒ x + 1/(x + 2) = 6
⇒ (x + 2) + 1/(x + 2) = 6 + 2
⇒ (x + 2) + 1/(x + 2) = 8
⇒ Let (x + 2) = y
⇒ y + 1/y = 8
⇒ Cubing both sides: (y + 1/y)³ = 8³
⇒ y³ + 1/y³ + 3 × y × (1/y) × (y + 1/y) = 512
⇒ y³ + 1/y³ + 3 × 1 × 8 = 512
⇒ y³ + 1/y³ + 24 = 512
⇒ y³ + 1/y³ = 512 − 24
⇒ y³ + 1/y³ = 488
⇒ (x + 2)³ + 1/(x + 2)³ = 488

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

**__Additional Information__**

Square Transformation

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Subtraction Case for Cubes

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Higher Power Transformation

If x + 1/x = k, then x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.</p

questions.question: From the summit of a 100 m high cliff, the angles of depression to two boats situated on the same side of the cliff are measured at 30° and 45° respectively. The boats are moving towards the cliff in a straight line. After 5 minutes, the angle of depression to the first boat becomes 60°, while the angle to the second boat becomes 75°. If both boats move at constant but different speeds, determine the initial distance between the two boats.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Distance (d) = Cliff Height × (cot θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ − cot θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ)

Here, Height = 100 m, θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ = 30°, θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ = 45°

d = 100 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

d = 100 × (√3 − 1) = 100 × (1.732 − 1) = 100 × 0.732

questions.question: If Y^x = 121 , what will (Y - 1)⁽x ⁻ ²⁾ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize 121 as 11², which gives Y = 11 and x = 2.

Substitute these values into (Y − 1)⁽x − ²⁾.

The expression becomes (11 − 1)⁽² − ²⁾ = 10⁰.

Since any number to the power 0 is 1, the result is 1.

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Yx = 121

Formula: If am = bⁿ, we can equate bases and exponents by expressing numbers in prime factor form.

⇒ Yx = 11²

⇒ Comparing both sides: Y = 11 and x = 2

⇒ Required value = (Y − 1)⁽x − ²⁾

⇒ (11 − 1)⁽² − ²⁾

⇒ 10⁰

⇒ 10⁰ = 1

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Zero Exponent Law

Any non-zero base raised to the power of zero is always equal to 1 (a⁰ = 1, where a ≠ 0).

Comparing Indices

If the bases are equal (ax = ay), then the exponents must be equal (x = y). If the exponents are equal (ax = bx), then the bases are equal (a = b).

Negative Exponents

A base with a negative exponent is equal to its reciprocal with a positive exponent: a−ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.</p

questions.question: A composite shape has a rectangle (10 cm × 4 cm) with a semicircle on one short side. What is the total area of the shape?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of composite shape = Area of Rectangle + Area of Semicircle

Area = (Length × Breadth) + (1/2 × π × r²)

Area = (10 × 4) + (0.5 × 3.14 × 2 × 2)

Area = 40 + 6.28 = 46.28 cm²

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Rectangle length (l) = 10 cm, Breadth (b) = 4 cm. Semicircle is on the short side (4 cm).

Formula Used: Area of Rectangle = l × b; Area of Semicircle = (π × r²) / 2

 
 

 
• 
 10 cm

 Rectangle

⇒ Area of the rectangle = 10 × 4 = 40 cm²

⇒ Diameter of the semicircle = Short side of rectangle = 4 cm

⇒ Radius (r) of the semicircle = 4 / 2 = 2 cm

⇒ Area of the semicircle = (3.14 × 2²) / 2 = (3.14 × 4) / 2

⇒ Area of the semicircle = 12.56 / 2 = 6.28 cm²

⇒ Total area of composite shape = 40 + 6.28 = 46.28 cm²

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of Semicircle

Area = (πr²) / 2 and Perimeter = πr + 2r (where 2r is the diameter).

Composite Shapes

To find the area of composite shapes, divide the shape into basic geometric forms like rectangles, triangles, and circles, then sum their individual areas.

Circle Constants

Value of π is approximately 3.14 or 22/7. For competitive exams, using 3.14 is often faster for decimal calculations.</p

questions.question: Complement of an angle is 12° more than twice the angle. Find the angle.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of an angle and its complement is always 90°.

Angle + (2 × Angle + 12°) = 90°

3 × Angle = 90° − 12° = 78°

Angle = 78° ÷ 3 = 26°

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Complement of angle = 2 × Angle + 12°

**Formula Used:**

Angle + Complement = 90°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required angle be x.

⇒ Its complement = 90° − x.

⇒ According to the question: 90° − x = 2x + 12°

⇒ 90° − 12° = 2x + x

⇒ 78° = 3x

⇒ x = 78° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 26°

**∴ The correct option is (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Two angles are called complementary if their sum is exactly 90°.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°.

Linear Pair

A pair of adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines that sum to 180°.

Reflex Angle

An angle which is greater than 180° but less than 360°.

Common triplet: (5, 12, 13), where 13 is the hypotenuse.

Trigonometric Identities

questions.question: In triangle ABC, the coordinates of vertices A and B are (0,0) and (6,0), respectively. Vertex C lies somewhere on the line y=x, and the centroid of triangle ABC is (5,3). What are the coordinates of point C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Centroid formula: ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3 , (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3)

C lies on y = x, so let C = (a, a).

⇒ (0 + 6 + a) ÷ 3 = 5 ⇒ 6 + a = 15 ⇒ a = 9

⇒ Hence C = (9, 9)

**∴ The correct answer is (9, 9) coordinates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

A = (0, 0), B = (6, 0)

Centroid = (5, 3)

C lies on y = x

Let coordinates of C be (x, x).

 
• 
• 
• y = x 
 A(0,0) B(6,0) C(9,9) G(5,3) 

Formula Used:

Centroid of triangle = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3 , (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3)

⇒ Using x-coordinate of centroid:

⇒ (0 + 6 + x) ÷ 3 = 5

⇒ 6 + x = 15

⇒ x = 9

⇒ Since C lies on y = x, y = 9

⇒ Coordinates of C = (9, 9)

**∴ The correct answer is (9, 9) coordinates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Centroid of Triangle

Centroid divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1. Formula = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) ÷ 3 , (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) ÷ 3).

Line y = x

Any point lying on y = x has equal coordinates. Example: (2,2), (5,5), (9,9).

Coordinate Geometry Shortcut

If two vertices and centroid are known, the third vertex can be found directly using x₃ = 3x̄ − x₁ − x₂.

Midpoint Formula

Midpoint of two points = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2 , (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2). It is frequently used with centroid and median problems.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line perpendicular to 7x+4y=6?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any line in the form ax + by = c, the slope of a perpendicular line is given by b/a.

In the equation 7x + 4y = 6, we have a = 7 and b = 4.

∴ The slope of the perpendicular line = b/a = 4/7.

In the given options, the date Sat Jul 04 represents 4/7 (4th day of the 7th month).

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Equation of the line is 7x + 4y = 6.

**Formula Used:** If a line has slope m₁, the slope of a perpendicular line m₂ satisfies m₁ × m₂ = −1.

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 7x + 4y = 6
 
• 
 m = 4/7
 

 Perpendicular lines have slopes m and −1/m

⇒ 7x + 4y = 6

⇒ 4y = −7x + 6

⇒ y = (−7/4)x + 6/4

⇒ Comparing with y = mx + c, the slope of the given line m₁ = −7/4

⇒ Let the perpendicular slope be m₂

⇒ m₁ × m₂ = −1

⇒ (−7/4) × m₂ = −1

⇒ m₂ = 4/7

**∴ The correct option is (3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slope of Parallel Lines

Two lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal, i.e., m₁ = m₂.

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation of a line with slope m and y-intercept c is y = mx + c.

General Equation Slope

For a linear equation in standard form Ax + By + C = 0, the slope is given by m = −A/B.

Product of Perpendicular Slopes

The product of slopes of two non-vertical perpendicular lines is always −1.</p

questions.question: If mean, median, and mode of a moderately skewed observations are (x - 1), (2x - 4) and '2x', respectively, then find the value of 'x'.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Empirical relation: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

2x = 3(2x − 4) − 2(x − 1)

2x = 6x − 12 − 2x + 2

2x = 4x − 10 ⇒ 2x = 10 ⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mean = (x − 1)

Median = (2x − 4)

Mode = 2x

**Formula Used:**

For a moderately skewed distribution: Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)

 
• Mean x − 1 Median 2x − 4 Mode 2x Empirical Relationship Scale 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ 2x = 3(2x − 4) − 2(x − 1)

⇒ 2x = 6x − 12 − 2x + 2

⇒ 2x = (6x − 2x) − (12 − 2)

⇒ 2x = 4x − 10

⇒ 10 = 4x − 2x

⇒ 10 = 2x

⇒ x = 10 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately skewed distribution, the distance between the mean and the median is about one-third of the distance between the mean and the mode.

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, Mean = Median = Mode. Any deviation from this equality indicates skewness.

Types of Skewness

If Mean > Median > Mode, it is positively skewed. If Mode > Median > Mean, it is negatively skewed.

questions.question: There are two circles with radii of 5 cm and 3 cm are positioned so that they touch each other internally. What is the distance between their centers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centers is the difference of their radii.

Distance (d) = R₁ − R₂

d = 5 − 3 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the first circle (R) = 5 cm

Radius of the second circle (r) = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

For two circles touching internally, distance between centers (d) = |R − r|

 
 
 
 C1
 
 C2
 
 P
 
• 
 
• 
 Radius R = 5 cm (C1 to P)
 Radius r = 3 cm (C2 to P)
 d = 2 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the centers be C₁ and C₂ and the point of contact be P.

⇒ C₁P = Radius 1 = 5 cm

⇒ C₂P = Radius 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Since they touch internally, centers and the point of contact are collinear.

⇒ Distance C₁C₂ = C₁P − C₂P

⇒ Distance = 5 − 3

⇒ Distance = 2 cm

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Externally Touching Circles

When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centers is the sum of their radii: d = R₁ + R₂.

Intersecting Circles

If two circles intersect at two distinct points, the distance between their centers (d) satisfies the condition: |R₁ − R₂| R₁ + R₂.</p
